input.quote: (a) EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF, CONTRACTOR'S MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO COMPANY ARISING FOR ANY REASON RELATING TO CONTRACTOR'S PERFORMANCE OF SERVICES UNDER A STATEMENT OF WORK SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH SERVICES. COMPANYS' MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO CONTRACTOR FOR ANY REASON ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR.
input.rationale: Section 7(a) caps both parties, so mutuality is satisfied, and 7(b) excludes lost profits and indirect/consequential damages mutually. The clause nonetheless fails the fallback on two material terms: (i) the basis is total fees paid for the relevant Services rather than 12 months' fees, so on a short or front-loaded engagement Contractor's exposure can fall below six months' fees; and (ii) there is no usable carve-out — the sole exception points to "PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF", which in this document is the Independent Contractor clause and not an indemnity, so indemnification, confidentiality breach, gross negligence and willful misconduct all sit inside the cap. Our edit re-bases both caps to fees paid in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim and adds a mutual, expressly uncapped Excluded Claims definition, while preserving the existing Paragraph 9 exception (which benefits us) verbatim. Contractor's cap remains scoped to Services under a Statement of Work while Company's covers the Agreement generally; that asymmetry favours us and is left unchanged. Preferred-only items (USD 1,000,000 floor, "paid or payable", data protection/security, fraud and IP carve-outs, and payment obligations outside the cap) are noted but not pressed.
